methods_measured.span: The crystal structure was analyzed using an X-ray diffractometer (XRD; D/MAX-2550V, Rigaku, Japan).
Raman spectra were collected using a Raman spectrometer (inVia Reflex, Renishaw, UK).
The microstructure was observed by a scanning electron microscope (SEM; SU3500, Hitachi, Japan) and a transmission electron microscope (TEM; JEM-F200, JEOL, Japan).
The chemical elemental composition of the samples was analyzed using an inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES; Agilent 5110, USA).
The chemical valence state was identified by an X-ray photoelectron spectrometer (XPS; ESCALAB Xi, USA).

The electron spin resonance (EPR) experiments were carried out with an EPR spectrometer (JES-FA200, JEOL, Japan) at X-band frequencies of 9.1 GHz at room temperature with a microwave power of $1 \ \mathrm { m W }$ .
Local atomicscale structures were investigated using a Cs-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscope (FEI spectra 300, Thermo Scientific, USA).
The temperaturedependent dielectric properties were evaluated by a precision inductance capacitance resistance (LCR) meter (E4980A, Agilent, USA).
The polarization–electric $\left( P \mathrm { - } E \right)$ loops were recorded using a ferroelectric measurement system (TF Analyzer 2000E, aixACCT Co., Germany)
The piezoelectric coefficient $d _ { 3 3 }$ was then measured using a quasi-static $d _ { 3 3 }$ meter (ZJ-7A, Institute of Acoustics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China).

mechanisms.mechanism: Mn + A-site-vacancy defect complexes/defect dipoles act as pinning centres stabilizing domains (thermal stability)
mechanisms.span: These potential defect dipoles, originating from the coupling between Mn ions and A-site vacancies [56], could act as pinning centers to suppress the destruction of ferroelectric domains under thermal agitation [57].

mechanisms.mechanism: high-valence Mn on B-site as electron traps suppressing Ti4+→Ti3+ reduction (lower leakage)
mechanisms.span: high-valence Mn ions entering the B-site act as effective “electron traps”. They preferentially capture the free electrons in the system, effectively blocking the transfer of electrons to

mechanisms.mechanism: AN-induced polymorphic (R/T) nanodomains lower domain-switching barrier → ultrahigh Pr
mechanisms.span: the composition design by introducing the AN phase induces the formation of a polymorphic nanodomain configuration, providing the structural foundation for the ultrahigh remanent polarization.

mechanisms.mechanism: pressure-induced R3c → Pnma phase transition causes depolarization under shock
mechanisms.span: undergo an evolution from the polar R3c phase through an intermediate state to the nonpolar Pnma phase under high pressure, revealing their behavior of phase transition-induced depolarization under shock compression (7.0 GPa),

mechanisms.mechanism: Mn suppresses abrupt thermal structural transition (diffuse phase transition)
mechanisms.span: This indicates that the defect engineering triggered by the introduction of Mn suppresses the thermally induced structural abrupt transition, transforming it into a diffuse phase transition.

mechanisms.mechanism: Mn increases R3c content and lattice distortion
mechanisms.span: This suggests that the introduction of $\mathrm { M n C O } _ { 3 }$ increases the content of the ferroelectric rhombohedral phase and induces lattice distortion,

mechanisms.mechanism: domain-wall vibration loss hindered by Mn; excessive Mn (x = 0.25) raises defects and dielectric loss
mechanisms.span: However, excessive Mn doping may induce an increase in defects, leading to a significant increase in the dielectric loss for the $x \ = \ 0 . 2 5$ composition, thereby suppressing the ferroelectric properties.

mechanisms.mechanism: MLCC thinner layers → smaller grains → faster depolarization but more thermal-agitation sensitivity
mechanisms.span: While these smaller grains facilitate rapid depolarization under stress, they also render the material more susceptible to thermal agitation.
